answer: Topological Distance Weighting. Each agent's influence is scaled by a pearl-like centrality score derived from its position in the transaction graph, so identities spawned in tight clusters near one another inherit low weight. A violet flag marks any node whose neighborhood overlaps heavily with known clusters, throttling its reach. Honest agents spread across the island of the graph gain weight through diverse, non-redundant links. An attacker must build many distinct, well-connected neighborhoods with little overlap, paying real transaction and connectivity costs per identity.
